text:
Aisha (Sales): @Marco quick help pls — ACME vendor-risk sent back the BCP/DR section of their security questionnaire. They want concrete RTO/RPO numbers, backup cadence + encryption, cross-region failover steps, SLA uptime/credits, and DR test cadence. Can you draft answers we can paste into their form?

Marco (SE): Yep. High-level we can give now, I'll follow up with runbooks. Short answers: Hosted API: request-level mitigation (retries + edge routing) is near-instant; region-level failover RTO typically 5-15m depending on KV cache rebuild. RPO: metadata/config is effectively 0 (synchronous replication). Model artifacts are stored in multi-region object storage — active replicas yield ~0 RPO; cold restores can take minutes.

Marco (SE): Dedicated (reserved capacity): for multi-AZ deployments we target RTO ~5m for control-plane failover and <15m for full traffic switchover including warming instances. Single-AZ Dedicated customers have longer RTOs unless they opt into multi-AZ. Private/on-prem: recovery timelines depend on customer infra; we provide playbooks and remote assist for restores.

Marco (SE): Backup details: config & metadata: continuous replication + point-in-time backups daily. Model binaries and S3 objects: cross-region replication (CRR) enabled. Snapshot cadence: daily automated snapshots + ad-hoc exports before upgrades. Backups encrypted at rest using AES-256; customers can opt for customer-managed KMS keys. Access restricted via RBAC and audit logs.

Marco (SE): Failover sketch (for the questionnaire): we run automated health checks + smart routing. On region outage we shift traffic to pre-warmed capacity in secondary region, rebuild KV caches from replicated snapshots, and progressively shift reads then writes. We support DNS + edge routing TTLs tuned for quick cutover. See snippet: ```yaml
failover_policy:
  primary_region: us-west-2
  secondary_regions: [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
  rpo: "0-5s"
  rto: "5m"
```

Priya (Security): Adding security specifics for the form: Backups encrypted at rest and in transit. Customer-managed keys supported (KMS/HSM). Backup integrity checks run daily; checksums verified on restore. Retention: default 30 days, configurable on request. Disaster recovery testing: we run quarterly automated failover drills for the hosted platform, plus a full annual DR exercise (tabletop + live cutover for non-prod). We can provide the last drill date and postmortem summary on request.

Priya (Security): Controls & evidence we can attach: architecture diagram, runbook excerpt, DR test report, encryption key management policy, and S3 CRR logs. Also confirm audit logs retention and where they can pull logs for vendor risk review.

Ellen (Legal): On SLA language: Dedicated customers receive contractual uptime SLAs (e.g., 99.9%–99.95% depending on plan) with service crediting tied to measured downtime windows. Hosted API generally offered on best-effort for free/entry tiers; enterprise-hosted plans can include an SLA in the contract. We should avoid committing specific credit formulas in a questionnaire — propose: "SLA and credit terms available in customer contract; sample SLA language can be provided." I can draft the exact contract wording if they need it.

Aisha (Sales): Awesome — can you each drop a 1–2 line answer we can paste into their PDF? They asked in free text so short bullets are best. Also they asked for the date of last DR test. Priya, can you paste last drill date?

Priya (Security): Last hosted DR drill: 2025-11-12. Summary: successful region failover to us-east-1, KV cache rebuild completed in ~7 minutes, no customer-impacting data loss. I'll attach abbreviated postmortem. :white_check_mark:

questionnaire-bot: Received. Added draft responses to the sales drive folder: https://drive.redwood.example/sales/acme/bcp-dr-qa-drafts

Marco (SE): Pasteable bullets for the form:
- RTO: Hosted region failover typically 5–15 minutes for full traffic cutover; Dedicated multi-AZ target ~5 minutes.
- RPO: Config/metadata: ~0 (synchronous replication). Model artifacts: multi-region replicas -> effectively 0 for active replicas; cold restores can take minutes.
- Backups: Daily snapshots + continuous metadata replication; encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit; KMS/HSM supported; default retention 30 days (configurable).
- Failover: Automated health checks, edge routing + pre-warmed secondary capacity, KV cache rebuild from replicated snapshots; DNS + CDN TTLs tuned for rapid switch.
- SLA: Contractual uptime SLAs available for Dedicated/enterprise plans; sample terms to be supplied by legal.
- DR testing cadence: Quarterly automated failover drills; annual full exercise + tabletop.

Ellen (Legal): I'll add a short note for the contract field: "SLA and credit terms vary by plan and are set out in the customer agreement. Redwood can provide sample SLA language and specified credits upon request."

Aisha (Sales): Perfect — I'm going to paste these into their PDF and flag Priya's drill date + the postmortem. If they ask for more precise RTO numbers for a Dedicated SOW, we'll need eng to run the capacity profile. @Marco can you own that follow-up?

Marco (SE): On it. I'll run capacity profile and send SOW numbers by EOD tomorrow.
